text: The Waterspring Field of Tanaris was named so because of the many water towers which pump the life-giving liquid from reserves deep underground. However, since the Cataclysm the entire field has been flooded from the South Seas.

Water elementals are elemental creatures made of water and various other liquids. On Azeroth, their domain on the Elemental Plane is known as the Abyssal Maw where they led by Neptulon the Tidehunter, while another group of water elementals serves one of the Abyssal Maw's creators, Helya, in the desolate realm of Helheim. Not all water elementals are minions of the elemental lords and princes, some are minions of the elemental spirits of Outland.
The Water of the Seers is provided as an objective for Rite of Vision (3). Consuming the waters will summon The Plains Vision.
Wavethrasher Scales drop from Wavethrashers, Young Wavethrashers, and Great Wavethrashers in Azshara.
Wavethrashers were hydras that lived off the coast of Azshara.
This item drops from Warlord Kalithresh in the Steamvault instance in heroic mode.

The remains of unfortunate shipping, prey to any number of disastrous events at sea. The bits of wreckage may circle the seas for many months before finally coming to rest just off shore in coastal regions, and one man's loss is another's gain. These circular water spawns function similarly to schools of fish (Oily Blackmouth, Firefin Snapper, etc), although the actual wreckage objects can make the circular boundary of them hard to spot. Wreckage usually spawns at the same places regular fish schools are found. They may be 'fished' to salvage bits of wreckage. If the bobber lands within the circle, successful fishing will produce watertight chests, which contain a random selection of items,
The Waterlogged Crate can be fished in Wetlands, Northern Stranglethorn, Ashenvale and Hillsbrad Foothills.
Waylay is a 2 point rogue talent located in the 2nd tier of the Subtlety tree.
The Waterweed Frond can be looted from Waterweed in the river below Zeb'Halak in the Grizzly Hills.

Water revenants are elemental revenants based around the element of water.

__NOTOC__ Wavespeaker Valoren is a draenei member of the Earthen Ring that is found in several locations in Vashj'ir. She is first found inside Nespirah (Alliance only), where she is rescued by the adventurer. She will help Alliance players with visions of the past. Valoren is later found in the Abyssal Depths where she gives a quest asking the player to aid and free the large whale, Wil'hai. She is also found in the Abyssal Maw, outside the entrance to Throne of the Tides where she allows players to get back out of that area by speaking to her.

Waterbearer's Robes are a quest reward from Wildmane Cleansing.

Wavespeaker Tulra is an Earthen Ring tauren shaman and a Horde quest giver located first at Nespirah, then in Legion's Rest, then appearing in several positions around the Abyssal Depths. She is interested in the Naz'jar Battlemaiden's past and in general the history of Vashj'ir, as evidenced by her constant request from players to enter the past and witness the Battlemaiden's visions. After the tragic Horde loss against the naga at the Ruins of Vashj'ir, she relocates to the Abyssal Depths and is concerned about the scalding shrooms of the area.

The Waterworks are one of the three capture points in the Battle for Gilneas battleground. It is located near the center of the map, parallel to the Overlook. Due to it being close to the Mines and the Lighthouse, it is often the base where most of the game's initial and late game combat takes place. The Waterworks has four points of entry, two on the Alliance side of the battleground and two on the Horde side. The Horde's entrances are through the waters of Waterworks, or by going around a cliff near the Mines, where one can find a Speed boost chest, and cross the river (the gap can be jumped and it is shallow enough to keep running on most mounts). The Alliance's entrances are by a broken
Water Warden is an elite unbound water elemental found in Halls of Origination.

:"Normally bugs are for bait, but how could you look into its eyes and even think that?" :-Nat Pagle Water striders are large water-bugs that make their first appearance with the World of Warcraft: Mists of Pandaria expansion. Water striders serve an important role in Jinyu culture, acting as a mount, means of sending communications, and even a family pet. They seem to be drawn to still water, and glow the brightest during spring. When preparing to travel to distant locations, Pandaren will traditionally capture a mirror strider and safely relocate it to another body of water.
__NOTOC__ Water Pincers can be found on the Singing Pools of the Wandering Isle. They can spit phlogiston and were regularly culled by Old Man Liang.

Waxwood, or Waxwood Forest, is a forest found to the northeast of Tian Monastery in north-central Jade Forest. It's here the Greenwood forest sprites reside. Guard Shan Long is found along the parameter of the forest and the monastery protecting the western entrance from the sprites and tigers, however, he feels that he will not be able to handle the tigers and asks stronger trainees to assist him.

Waterspeaker Gorai is a jinyu waterspeaker found at Inkgill Mere of Kun-Lai Summit. When Elder Shai Hu drank the sha-corrupted waters of the mere, and forced the others to do the same, Gorai protested. Orachi of the town guard confiscated Gorai's ritual staff and banished him. The adventurers of the Horde and Alliance assisted him in retaking his village from sha-corrupted jinyu, cleansing the mere, and fighting the corrupter, Shai Hu. At some point, the Kor'kron captured him and some fellow waterspeakers, then placed them into a cage in the Menagerie below Orgrimmar along with other various creatures and races from Pandaria. Watertaster Kurashel is a random jinyu traveler who will occasionally appear at the Halfhill Market in the Valley of the Four Winds. He can be seen investigating the pond next to Jogu the Drunk. The pond contains fish corpses.

The Waterlogged Zandalari Journal is a rare drop from Zandalari trolls in Za'Tual, the Beast Pens, and the Conqueror's Terrace on the Isle of Thunder. It contains a first-hand account of the damaging of Zandalar during the Cataclysm. Looting this book is one of the requirements of the Pandaria quest achievement Zandalari Library Card.

The Way of the Brew is a style of Pandaren cooking mastered by Bobo Ironpaw. The recipes do not focus on any stat, but allow the creation of several unique alcoholic brews which can increase stats or cause amusing side effects. In order to learn the Way of the Brew, the character must have 525 cooking skill and complete Ready for Greatness, then Way of the Brew (quest). Obtaining 600 skill points in Way of the Brew cooking awards the achievement Master of the Brew, which is part of the achievement Master of Pandaren Cooking.

The Way of the Oven is a style of Pandaren cooking mastered by Jian Ironpaw. The recipes focus on increasing stamina, making this an optimal Way for Protection Warriors, Protection Paladins, Guardian Druids, Blood Death Knights, and Brewmaster Monks. In order to learn the Way of the Oven, the character must have 525 cooking skill and complete Ready for Greatness, then Way of the Oven (quest). Obtaining 600 skill points in Way of the Oven cooking awards the achievement Master of the Oven, which is part of the achievement Master of Pandaren Cooking.

The Way of the Steamer is a style of Pandaren cooking mastered by Yan Ironpaw. The recipes focus on increasing spirit, making this an optimal Way for Discipline/Holy Priests, Restoration Druids, Elemental/Restoration Shamans, Holy Paladins, and Mistweaver Monks. In order to learn the Way of the Steamer, the character must have 525 cooking skill and complete Ready for Greatness, then Way of the Steamer (quest). Obtaining 600 skill points in Way of the Steamer cooking awards the achievement Master of the Steamer, which is part of the achievement Master of Pandaren Cooking.

The Way of the Pot is a style of Pandaren cooking mastered by Mei Mei Ironpaw. The recipes focus on increasing intellect, making this an optimal Way for Mages, Warlocks, Priests, Balance/Restoration Druids, Restoration/Elemental Shamans, Holy Paladins, and Mistweaver Monks. In order to learn the Way of the Pot, the character must have 525 cooking skill and complete Ready for Greatness, then Way of the Pot (quest). Obtaining 600 skill points in Way of the Pot cooking awards the achievement Master of the Pot, which is part of the achievement Master of Pandaren Cooking.

The Way of the Wok is a style of Pandaren cooking mastered by Anthea Ironpaw. The recipes focus on increasing agility, making this an optimal Way for Rogues, Hunters, Feral/Guardian Druids, Enhancement Shamans, and Windwalker/Brewmaster Monks. In order to learn the Way of the Wok, the character must have 525 cooking skill and complete Ready for Greatness, then Way of the Wok (quest). Obtaining 600 skill points in Way of the Wok cooking awards the achievement Master of the Wok, which is part of the achievement Master of Pandaren Cooking.

Watergliding Jets is an engineer-only permanent "enchant" to the engineer's belt. It will give a 12 second speed increase, while swimming, every 30 seconds. It can only be applied to a belt in the engineer's inventory, and applying it will cause the belt to become soulbound.

She was the one who searched for Sharas'dal, Scepter of Tides, but was unfortunately captured when she tracked the staff to the Abyssal Maw. She was later rescued by Erunak Stonespeaker, the Farseer and Grash and together they claimed the staff from Lady Zithreen. She is later found in the Heart of Azeroth.

Weaponsmithing was one of two primary blacksmithing specializations (the other being Armorsmithing) which allowed access to certain BoP weapon recipes. Weaponsmithing was required to access any of the weapon sub-specialties: Axe-, Hammer-, or Swordsmithing. Weaponsmithing was granted from the quest The Way of the Weaponsmith. It was available from at the Great Forge in Ironforge, and in Orgrimmar.
__NOTOC__ Weak Flux is used by Blacksmiths to purge metals of impurities while they are forged into an item. The most common type of flux in iron and steel furnaces is limestone.

Weather effects are ambient graphics that appear in-game that simulate real weather. In patch 1.10 rainfall, snowstorms and sandstorms were added to various zones in World of Warcraft. For several years after being added, weather had no gameplay effect. With the introduction of the Pet Battle System in Mists of Pandaria, some capturable battle pets now only appear during specific weather.

Weapon type is the general category any weapon falls into for the purposes of the associated combat skill: * 1H axe * 2H axe * Bow * Crossbow * Dagger * Fishing pole * Fist weapon * Gun * 1H mace * 2H mace * Polearm * Stave * 1H sword * 2H sword * Thrown weapon * Wand

The Weathered Nook was a small, well-hidden cave and home to Dorn Plainstalker and Prate Cloudseer, found on the northern wall of Thousand Needles. It was flooded during the cataclysm, it's unknown if Dorn and Prate survived.
Weapon Expertise is a tier 6 talent in the Combat rogue tree. Maxing it requires a total of 27 points in Combat.

Weazel's Crater is a large, deep crater located in the northern part of the Shimmering Flats. Its origins are mysterious, but its name suggests either who found it or who created it. Due to the fact that there are often goblin and gnome races around the area in highly dangerous cars (as seen by the many bits of rubble and craters scattered about) perhaps this is a result from a rather unstable invention. It's currently inhabited by Saltstone basilisks.

Weapon speed is a number that represents the relative speed of a weapon to other weapons. Like attack speed, the lower the number the greater actual speed of the attack, so the number should be interpreted more like a delay number.
Weather-Worn Boots are a quest reward from Princess Must Die!
